_comment: Why a session is calling the operator, as a closed vocabulary of codes (#742).
The daemon derives it and ships it in the session view (`attention_reason`),
the same way it derives the attention set itself (ADR-0011, #617): which of
these applies is a decision about the session, and a decision belongs on the
server or the three clients disagree — the dashboard had already dropped
`error` from its own attention list once (#538).
The *sentence* is not here, deliberately. The server sends a code, never prose:
RFC 9457 provides a human-readable field and tells consumers not to act on it,
because prose emitted by the server fixes the language and the register for
every client at once. And the three surfaces should not read alike — the GNOME
toast names the machine and the branch because it carries no other context,
where the TUI has the board on screen. Each client writes its own wording; this
file pins what they must all be able to say something about.
`call` outranks the rest: the session said so itself, where `waiting` and
`error` are deductions (ADR-0010). Read by internal/status/reason_test.go and

reasons.why: the session raised a call for the operator
the session is blocked on an answer from the operator
the session stopped on a live Claude API error
